paper.title: Algorithm 468: Algorithm for Automatic Numerical Integration Over a Finite Interval
paper.venue: Communications of the ACM 16(11), 694 (CALGO Algorithm 468; netlib version carries the TOMS-era test program)

code.commit: netlib TOMS archive 468.gz: one Fortran text file with the routines QUAD and QSUB and the test programs TEST01, TEST02 and TEST03
code.archive: sha256 1891044f1acedad241f46b6e1a16b0803ab3a2c54b37fbab333665a755d82319 (netlib.org/toms/468.gz as downloaded 2026-11-26, 13609 bytes); uncompressed text sha256 aeb697834d6b689202cdd825d9cfad5f25c61c6ebeb791b2023874660110f73b
code.note: Single-file Fortran (free-form comments, REAL arithmetic). The file contains its own main program (line 69, program main) calling TEST01, TEST02, TEST03. Build with gfortran; expect -std=legacy or -ffixed-line-length warnings.

claim.location: TEST01 in the archive's own test program: for 13 integrands f01..f13 it calls QUAD with the requested relative accuracy EPSIL = 0.001 and prints the computed result next to a hard-coded exact value. Registered: f07, f08, f12 and f13 from TEST01. For f13 on [0,1] the source comments that the reference's exact value 0.0013492485650 'is apparently a typo' and uses 0.013492485650; that corrected value is the registered one.
claim.metric: result(k) printed by TEST01 for each registered integrand, compared with the exact value in the source
claim.paper_value: QUAD integral of f07 on [0, 1] = 0.7775046341; QUAD integral of f08 on [0.1, 1] = 0.009098645256; QUAD integral of f12 on [0, 1] = -0.6346651825; QUAD integral of f13 on [0, 1] = 0.01349248565

tolerance.abs: per value, in values[].tol_abs (1e-3 times the exact value)
tolerance.basis: Fixed before any run. The documentation of QUAD (EPSIL: 'relative accuracy required') guarantees a relative error not exceeding EPSIL when the routine reports success (ICHECK = 0), and TEST01 sets EPSIL = 0.001, so the registered tolerance is the algorithm's own contract and no looser. The run must also report ICHECK = 0 for the registered integrands. Not to be loosened after any run.

cost.data_licence: No data. Licence not stated in the archive; the rerun should record it.

why: A 1973 adaptive quadrature routine ships a 13-integrand test program with hard-coded exact answers, including one where the original reference had a typo. The code must compute every integral, so the claim tests the oldest code in the batch against its own published accuracy contract.
